newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Foreign bank eyeing Nordbanken buy - paper.
newsitem.headline: Foreign bank eyeing Nordbanken buy - paper.

text.p: A foreign bank has approached the Swedish government, showing its interest in buying state-controlled bank Nordbanken, a domestic financial daily reported on Wednesday.
"A large foreign bank has informed the government about its interest in Nordbanken," Finanstidningen said.
The government was contacted after merger talks between Nordbanken and S-E-Banken failed at the beginning of February when S-E-Banken pulled out.
The banks did not give any reason for the failure, but analysts said S-E-Banken's management could not accept that Nordbanken wanted both the chief executive and chairman posts.
Nordbanken's chief executive, the government and S-E-Banken owners have said they are sorry the deal did not go through and market players are speculating on another round of merger talks.
"According to other information, not yet confirmed, an insurance company also has shown interest for some kind of coordination with Nordbanken," Finanstidningen added.

The paper did not find it likely that the government would sell its stake of just below 60 percent in Nordbanken, worth roughly 28 billion crowns ($3.8 billion), to a foreign player as long as there was a chance that Nordbanken and S-E-Banken could resume talks.
"Probably the government would prefer a merger between Nordbanken and S-E-Banken over selling its stake to a foreign bank," the newspaper said.
"A merger between the two Swedish commercial banks could create a competitive alternative to the new banking groups -- Handelsbanken-Stadshypotek and Swedbank-Foreningsbanken."
Swedish banks Swedbank and Foreningsbanken announced this month that they would merge and banking group Handelsbanken finalised its 22.9 billion crown bid for mortgage bank Stadshypotek in February.
"A merger between Nordbanken and for example a German or Dutch bank is a completely different deal from a merger of two Swedish commercial banks," the newspaper said.
Such a merger would not create cost synergies on the domestic market where Nordbanken is mainly active and it would not strengthen Nordbanken domestically, the newspaper said.
Nordbanken's share rose nine crowns to 274 on Tuesday.
-- Birgitta Forsberg, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1006 ($ = 7.419 Swedish Crowns)
